title: General divisors irreducible simultaneously on a finite etale cover
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, $X$ a smooth connected affine $k$-scheme of finite type and pure dimension $d\ge2$, and $\pi:T\to X$ a finite etale morphism with $T$ connected. Let $S\subset X(k)$ be a nonempty finite set. Let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module, $V$ a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space, and $\psi:V\to\Gamma(X,L)$ a $k$-linear map. Assume all $\psi(v)$ vanish on the reduced subscheme $S$, their restrictions generate $L|_{X\setminus S}$, and the associated morphism $X\setminus S\to\mathbf P(V)$ is an immersion. For $v\in V$ set $H_v=Z(\psi(v))$ and $T_v=T\times_X H_v$. There is a nonempty Zariski open $U_{\rm irr}\subseteq\mathbf A(V)$ such that both $H_v$ and $T_v$ are geometrically irreducible over $k$ for every $v\in U_{\rm irr}(k)$. For such a $v$, if $H_v$ is smooth over $k$, then $T_v$ is smooth over $k$, and $T_v\to H_v$ is a finite etale morphism between connected schemes. Here $\mathbf A(V)$ is affine space with $k$-points $V$. Scheme and morphism notions are those of [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]; invertible sheaves, generation, associated projective morphisms, zero schemes, base change and connectedness are as in [def-sc-invertible-module], [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections], [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections], [def-pc-zero-scheme], [def-pc-base-change] and [def-weil-connected-scheme]; geometric irreducibility is as in [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]; pure dimension is as in [def-weil-pure-dimension].

proof.text: Write $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$. By [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], $T=\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B$ finite as an $A$-module. If $a_1,\ldots,a_m$ generate $A$ over $k$ and $b_1,\ldots,b_n$ generate $B$ as an $A$-module, these elements together generate $B$ as a $k$-algebra: every element of $B$ is an $A$-linear combination of the $b_j$. Thus $T$ is affine of finite type over $k$. Form $L_T=\pi^*L$ and the linear map $\psi_T(v)=\pi^*\psi(v)$ using the tensor formula in [def-pc-module-pullback]. A local frame $e$ of $L$ pulls back to a frame $1\otimes e$ of $L_T$, so it is invertible. Etaleness includes flatness by [def-weil-etale-morphism]; hence [lem-pc-zero-scheme-properties] identifies $Z(\psi_T(v))$ with $T\times_X H_v=T_v$.

source.place: Tags 01WH (definition-integral), 02GI (definition-etale); zero schemes on trivializing affine opens

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres], $\pi$ is smooth. Its composition with the smooth map $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth by [lem-trf-smooth-composition], so both $X$ and $T$ are smooth over $k$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular] to each, then [lem-sc-regular-connected-integral] using their assumed nonempty connectedness. Both schemes are integral; in particular $A$ and $B$ are domains by [def-pc-integral-scheme].

source.place: Tag 056S (lemma-smooth-regular); properties.tex Tags 0569 and 033N; morphisms.tex Tag 01VA

proof.text: Every finite separable field extension $E/k$ is isomorphic to $k$ over $k$: the minimal polynomial of each element splits over the algebraically closed field $k$ and, being irreducible, is linear. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_kE)$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_kE)$ are isomorphic to the integral, hence irreducible schemes $X$ and $T$. Apply [lem-zl-geometric-irreducibility-finite-separable-test] separately to $A$ and $B$. It follows that $X$ and $T$ are geometrically irreducible over $k$.

Every closed point of either finite-type $k$-scheme has residue field finite over $k$ by [lem-kun-closed-point-field], hence equal to $k$. A $k$-rational point maps to a $k$-rational, therefore closed, point under $\pi$. Since $X$ is integral of pure dimension $d$, $\dim A=d$ by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-topological-krull-dimension-ring]. For every closed $x\in X$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-domain-dimension-local-ring-localization] gives $\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}=d$. For every closed $t\in T$, with $x=\pi(t)$, the affine etale ring map $A\to B$ gives $\dim\mathcal O_{T,t}=\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}=d$ by [lem-sc-etale-local-dimension]. Finally [lem-sc-scheme-stalk-dimension-generalization-chains] identifies these dimensions with $\operatorname{codim}(\{x\},X)$ and $\operatorname{codim}(\{t\},T)$.

The support of the common zero scheme on $X$ is exactly $S$: all sections vanish on $S$, and at every point outside $S$ some section is nonzero in the fibre by [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-generating-sections-fibre]. On $T$ the support is exactly $\pi^{-1}S$, since locally the pullback ideal is generated by the images of the same finitely many section coefficients. This asserts equality of supports, without asserting that the base schemes are reduced. Each fibre over $s\in S$ has dimension zero by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres] and is affine of finite type over $k$ (its ring is $B\otimes_A k$). By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-dim-zero-artinian] it has finitely many points. These points are $k$-rational and closed in $T$ by the preceding step. Thus both base supports are finite sets of closed points, and all their irreducible components have codimension $d\ge2$ by the preceding step. This verifies hypothesis (ii) of [lem-zl-bertini-irreducible-member] for both systems.

The open $T\setminus\pi^{-1}S$ is nonempty. Otherwise the underlying space of the nonempty scheme $T$ would be a finite set of closed points, with no strict generalizations; [lem-sc-scheme-stalk-dimension-generalization-chains] would give dimension zero for all its local rings, contrary to dimension $d\ge2$ at closed points. By [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space], closed points are dense in $T$, so choose a closed $t$ in this open and set $x=\pi(t)$. Both are $k$-rational and $x\notin S$.

Choose $v_1\in V$ with $s_1=\psi(v_1)$ nonzero at $x$, using [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-generating-sections-fibre], and extend $v_1$ to a basis $v_1,e_2,\ldots,e_r$ of $V$. Near $x$, use $s_1$ as frame and put $a_i=\psi(e_i)/s_1$. By [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections] and [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts], these are the pullbacks of the polynomial coordinates $T_i/T_1$ on the corresponding affine chart. The assumed immersion gives a surjection from the local ring of projective space at the image of $x$ onto $\mathcal O_{X,x}$: factor it as an open immersion after a closed immersion and use [def-weil-closed-immersion]. It therefore gives a surjection on maximal ideals modulo their squares. The maximal ideal of the chart at this $k$-point is generated by $T_i/T_1-a_i(x)$ (subtracting a polynomial's value expresses it in these generators). Consequently the classes of $a_i-a_i(x)$ span $\mathfrak m_x/\mathfrak m_x^2$. They are the local coefficients of $\psi(w_i)$, where $w_i=e_i-a_i(x)v_1$ vanishes at $x$.

source.place: Tags 01NE and 01NF (projective space by sections and its charts); morphisms.tex Tag 01QO

proof.text: For each of the two regular local rings $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and $R=\mathcal O_{T,t}$, let $\mathfrak m$ be its maximal ideal and put $e=\dim_k\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$. Regularity and $\dim R=d$ imply $e\le d$ by [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Lift a basis of this cotangent space to $e$ elements of $\mathfrak m$; they generate $\mathfrak m$ by [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators], since $\mathfrak m$ is finite over the Noetherian ring $R$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-height-quotient-bound] with $J=\mathfrak P=\mathfrak m$ gives $d\le e$, since $R/\mathfrak m=k$ has height zero. Hence $e=d$ for both local rings.

source.place: Tag 00DV (lemma-NAK); regular local ring definition and the Noetherian height bound

proof.text: Because $\pi$ is etale it is unramified by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. At the rational points $t,x$, [lem-sc-rational-unramified-cotangent-criterion] gives a surjection $\mathfrak m_x/\mathfrak m_x^2\to\mathfrak m_t/\mathfrak m_t^2$. Thus the pulled-back classes of $a_i-a_i(x)$ span the latter space, of dimension $d\ge2$. Choose two $k$-linear combinations of the $w_i$, denoted $v_2,v_3$, whose pulled-back coefficients have independent cotangent classes at $t$. Their coefficients at $x$ are also independent, since any relation at $x$ would pull back to a relation at $t$. The sections $\psi(v_2),\psi(v_3)$ vanish at $x$, their pullbacks vanish at $t$, and $\psi(v_1)$ and its pullback are nonzero at these points.

In each local ring $R$ of step 8, let $f,g$ be the coefficients of these two sections in the frame $\psi(v_1)$ or its pullback. Their independent classes extend to a basis of $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$; lifting the rest and applying [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] extends $f,g$ to a minimal set of $d$ generators of $\mathfrak m$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence], $R/(f)$ and $R/(f,g)$ are regular local rings of dimensions $d-1,d-2$. By [lem-sc-regular-local-domain], they and $R$ are domains. Thus $(0)\subsetneq(f)\subsetneq\mathfrak p=(f,g)$ is a strict chain of prime ideals: $f\ne0$ and $g\notin(f)$ follow from their independent cotangent classes. The height of $\mathfrak p$ is at least two. It is at most two by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-height-quotient-bound] with $J=\mathfrak P=\mathfrak p$ and two generators, because $\mathfrak P/J=0$ has height zero in the domain $R/\mathfrak p$. Hence $\operatorname{ht}_R(\mathfrak p)=2$.

source.place: Tags 00DV (lemma-NAK), 00NQ (lemma-regular-ring-CM), 00NP (lemma-regular-domain) and the Noetherian height bound

proof.text: For each pair $(Y,y)=(X,x),(T,t)$ choose an affine neighbourhood $W=\operatorname{Spec}C$ on which the chosen frame is invertible; write the section coefficients as $f,g\in C$ and $R=C_{\mathfrak m_y}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-primes-of-localization], the prime $(f,g)R$ contracts to a prime $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak m_y$ of $C$. It is minimal over $(f,g)C$: a smaller prime containing this ideal would extend to a smaller prime containing the prime ideal $(f,g)R$, which is impossible. The same inclusion-preserving prime correspondence identifies all chains below $\mathfrak q$ with chains below $(f,g)R$, so $\operatorname{ht}_C\mathfrak q=2$. By [lem-pc-zero-scheme-properties] and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes], $V(\mathfrak q)$ is an irreducible component of the intersection of the two zero schemes inside $W$.

source.place: Tags 00E3 (lemma-spec-localization) and 00ES (lemma-irreducible, minimal-prime components), applied to the quotient C/(f,g)

proof.text: Take the closure $Z_Y$ of this component in the global intersection $Z(\psi_Y(v_2))\cap Z(\psi_Y(v_3))$. The open-subspace correspondence [lem-weil-pbc-open-subspace-irreducible-closed-correspondence] preserves strict inclusions and shows that this closure is an irreducible component of the global intersection. It contains $y$. At its generic point its codimension in $Y$ is two, by [lem-sc-scheme-stalk-dimension-generalization-chains] and the height calculation of step 11. Since $\psi_Y(v_1)$ is nonzero at $y$, this component is not contained in $Z(\psi_Y(v_1))$. Thus hypothesis (i) of [lem-zl-bertini-irreducible-member] holds on both $X$ and $T$, with the same $v_1,v_2,v_3$.

Apply [lem-zl-bertini-irreducible-member] to $(X,L,V,\psi)$ and $(T,L_T,V,\psi_T)$. Finite type and geometric irreducibility were established in steps 1--3, condition (ii) in step 5, and condition (i) in step 12. The precise meaning of general in that lemma yields nonempty Zariski opens $U_X,U_T\subseteq\mathbf A(V)$ such that $H_v$ and $T_v$, respectively, are geometrically irreducible on these opens. Their parameter spaces are the same: the pullback system has domain $V$, even if a linear map of sections has a kernel.

Set $U_{\rm irr}=U_X\cap U_T$. In any basis the coordinate ring of $\mathbf A(V)$ is a polynomial ring over $k$, a domain by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-domain]. Its nilradical is the proper prime ideal $(0)$, so [lem-zl-spectrum-irreducible-nilradical-prime] makes its spectrum irreducible. Hence the two nonempty opens meet. For every $v\in U_{\rm irr}(k)$ both schemes are geometrically irreducible, as required. In particular they are nonempty and connected, by specializing geometric irreducibility to $k$ and using that two disjoint nonempty clopen pieces would contradict irreducibility.

source.place: Tag 0G4F, intersecting the two general conditions; polynomial domain and irreducibility definitions

proof.text: The morphism $T_v\to H_v$ is the base change of the finite etale morphism $\pi$, hence is finite etale by the base-change functor of [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category]. If $H_v$ is smooth over $k$, then $T_v\to H_v$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres], and $T_v\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth by [lem-trf-smooth-composition]. The connectedness of both schemes was proved in step 14. This gives every clause of the final assertion.

source.place: Tags 01WL (finite base change), 02GO (etale base change), 02GK (etale implies smooth), 01VA (smooth composition)

split_report.summary: Proved the original statement with no change and no new nodes. Reused the existing Bertini criterion and supplied its hypotheses on both schemes using regular local rings, the rational unramified cotangent criterion, Nakayama, height bounds and localization prime correspondence. Distinguished the support of the finite base locus from its possibly nonreduced scheme structure. Checked the actual project Bertini declaration, which is sorried and is a different statement. Repair after live-DAG promotion refusal: rebased the retained split onto the current unsplit item; compared all 36 cited statements with the retained full-statement citation quotes (all unchanged), rechecked every use and replaced the generic off-unit tool explanations with step-specific justifications. Retained the statement, all 15 proof steps, citation evidence and actual search log.

tool_uses.why: Steps 1 and 11 use the flat-base-change identity and the affine quotient description of zero schemes. These are generic zero-scheme tools, not a different Bertini route; this unit has no lemma giving those formulas.

Steps 2, 5 and 15 use that an etale morphism is smooth and its fibres have dimension zero, to obtain regularity, finite base support and conditional smoothness upstairs. This unit has no such general etale geometry lemma.
Step 2 uses regularity of every local ring of a smooth scheme over a field. The unit has no general smooth-to-regular statement; this supplies local algebra for the prescribed Bertini argument.

Step 2 uses integrality of a nonempty connected regular scheme on both X and T. This is the general scheme-theoretic input for the blueprint sentence that both are irreducible; no statement in this unit supplies it.

Step 4 uses that closed points of finite-type schemes over k have residue fields finite over k, and that rational points are closed. This checks the rational-point hypotheses of the local cotangent tool; the unit has no closed-point field lemma.

Step 4 uses equality of the dimensions of a finite-type domain and its localization at any maximal ideal. This checks codimensions and cotangent dimensions at closed points, rather than replacing any unit-level argument.
Step 4 uses equality of local-ring dimensions along an etale ring map to obtain dimension d at closed points of T. The unit has no general dimension comparison for etale morphisms.

Steps 5 and 7 use the equivalence between generation of an invertible sheaf and some section being nonzero in every fibre. This identifies the base support and selects a frame; the unit contains no fibrewise generation criterion.

Step 7 uses polynomial affine coordinates and the section-ratio formulas on a projective chart to deduce cotangent spanning from the assumed immersion. This coordinate tool is not supplied by a statement of this unit.

Step 9 uses cotangent surjectivity for an unramified morphism at rational points. This proves that the same two section coefficients give independent directions upstairs; the unit contains no unramified cotangent criterion.
Step 10 uses regularity and dimension d-c of the quotients by the first c parameters. This is the local algebra proving the codimension-two witness in the blueprint, not a new Bertini conclusion.
